points.description: States that linked lists can be of variable length, i.e. they can grow and shrink dynamically (size not fixed in advance), using precise terms such as 'variable length' / 'dynamic size'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit (1.5) if only a loosely related statement is given, e.g. 'flexible size' or 'no need to declare size' without saying length can change/vary.

points.description: Correctly contrasts with arrays: arrays have a fixed length (size fixed at declaration/creation), whereas linked lists do not.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact that linked lists have variable (dynamic) length, plus the contrast that arrays are fixed in size. Vague claims (e.g. 'more efficient', 'faster', 'uses less memory') earn nothing. Any wrong claim, such as linked lists having faster random access, removes the point it relates to.
